correctness.rationale: Inspected the actual RESULT.md proof and verify_subdivision.py graph construction. The false-twin classes A\{a0}, B\{b0} each force at most one initially white vertex in any forcing set, since any twin pair is a fort. With x=a0,y=b0,t=s,u in A\{a0},v in B\{b0}, direct neighborhood checks show {x,t,u}, {y,t,v} and {x,y,u,v} are forts. Every four-white choice among representatives contains one of these, so admissible white sets have at most three vertices. Exactly eight types of three whites avoid the obstruction patterns; the explicit force schedules in RESULT.md are valid with p,q≥3 because alternative blue twin-class vertices exist. By monotonicity, all their subsets force, giving a necessary and sufficient avoidance criterion. Any nonforcing white set contains a listed fort, and listed forts are incomparable, so five families exhaust inclusion-minimal forts. Counting admissible whites at sizes 0,1,2,3 gives the displayed complete polynomial. Fresh independent direct zero-forcing simulation enumerated all 2^(p+q+1) white sets and minimal forts for (p,q)=(3,3),(3,4),(4,4), obtaining coefficient vectors [21,19,7,1], [29,24,8,1], [40,30,9,1] at increasing forcing sizes and 10,15,21 minimal forts respectively. Those bounded tests corroborate the symbolic infinite-family proof.
residual_risks: The explicit eight-type forcing schedules require at least one initially blue alternative in each twin class; this is why the p,q≥3 boundary is essential.
Finite enumeration covers three small pairs only; classification for every p,q uses the fort and forcing-schedule proof.

value.rationale: Single-edge subdivision is a canonical local graph transformation. Beyond a routine minimum value, this theorem gives the complete all-cardinality zero-forcing distribution and a minimal-fort obstruction hypergraph on an infinite two-parameter family, quantifying a sharp increase from pq to 3pq-p-q optimum sets despite an unchanged minimum size. Exact fort families and the count can be independently used in transversal, forcing and graph-operation comparisons; the all-coefficient and structural classification has substantive natural motivation.
residual_risks: No statement for p<3, q<3, multiple or total-edge subdivisions; those require distinct classifications.

final_claim: For p,q>=3, let H_{p,q} replace one edge a_0 b_0 of K_{p,q} by the two edges a_0 s, s b_0. Its ordinary zero-forcing polynomial is Z(H;z)=z^(p+q-2)[(3pq-p-q)+(pq+2p+2q-2)z+(p+q+1)z^2+z^3]. The complete inclusion-minimal fort family consists of twin pairs in A\{a0}, twin pairs in B\{b0}, {a0,s,u}, {b0,s,v}, and {a0,b0,u,v} with u in A\{a0}, v in B\{b0}; hence Z(H)=p+q-2 and there are 3pq-p-q minimum zero-forcing sets.
limitations: Finite direct enumeration covers p,q in {(3,3),(3,4),(4,4)} only, not the entire infinite family.
